svg.title: P24 anytime-valid adaptive physical-refinement certification
svg.desc: Publication-style theorem map for time-uniform base-law confidence, adaptive descriptor selection, and finite stopping-time validity.
svg.text: P24 · Anytime-Valid Adaptive Physical-Refinement Certification
A summable error schedule turns the fixed-sample P23 certificate into one event valid at every positive sample size.
ALPHA SPENDING ACROSS TIME
Allocate the total failure budget over all positive sample sizes
αₙ = 6α/(π²n²)
Σₙ≥1 αₙ = α
Each fixed-time base-law certificate uses its own local level αₙ.
TIME-UNIFORM BASE EVENT
One confidence event holds simultaneously for every n
τₙany(α) = min{1, (M/2)√[(1/(2n)) log(Mπ²n²/(3α))]}
Pr(∀n ≥ 1: ‖P − P̂ₙ‖TV ≤ τₙany) ≥ 1 − α
A countable union bound over the local failures produces the anytime-valid event.
ADAPTIVE DESCRIPTOR SELECTION
P23 now holds at every time simultaneously
f̂ₙ = Sₙ(Z₁,…,Zₙ)
The selected gain and residual inherit valid intervals for every n.
No new candidate-count union bound is introduced.
FINITE STOPPING-TIME VALIDITY
Repeated inspection no longer breaks nominal coverage
τ = data-dependent stopping time
Because the event holds for all n, it also holds at the realized finite τ.
Examples include first positive gain or first small-regret certificate.
ANYTIME NEAR-OPTIMALITY
The P23 refinement-regret certificate is valid at every time and at stopping
0 ≤ G* − Gf̂ₙ ≤ Bₙ
Rf̂ₙ − minf Rf = G* − Gf̂ₙ ≤ Bₙ
METHOD BOUNDARY
Conservative alpha spending; not an optimal martingale or e-process bound.
INTERPRETATION BOUNDARY
Anytime validity is not physical completeness and is not an experiential theorem.
